sections.content: You know *No es que* + subjunctive, *sino que* + indicative from B2 Unit 5: it rejects a reason someone might assume and gives the real one. At C1 an editorial uses it for something bigger. It rejects how the other side *reads* your position and puts your own reading in its place: *No es que se pretenda restringir el comercio, sino que se busca ordenar la circulación*. You do not attack a person. You correct a misreading. Put the rejected reading in a short first part and give the real one more weight in the second, which may be longer.

sections.title: The pattern, present and past
rows: No es que la medida sea mala, sino que llega tarde.
It is not that the measure is bad; it is that it comes too late.
No es que se pretenda restringir el comercio, sino que se busca ordenar la circulación.
It is not that anyone means to restrict trade; it is that they want to bring order to the traffic.
No era que los comerciantes se opusieran al cambio, sino que temían perder clientes.
It was not that the shopkeepers opposed the change; it was that they feared losing customers. (past: imperfect subjunctive, then imperfect)

items.spanish: No es que el editorial rechace el diálogo, sino que exige resultados.
items.english: It is not that the editorial rejects dialogue, but that it demands results.

items.spanish: No es que los vecinos quieran el ruido, sino que nadie les ofrece otra solución.
items.english: It is not that the residents want the noise, but that nobody offers them another solution.

items.spanish: No es que el comerciante cuestione el plan, sino que pide más tiempo.
items.english: It is not that the shopkeeper challenges the plan, but that he asks for more time.

items.spanish: No era que el ayuntamiento malinterpretara las quejas, sino que no quería escucharlas.
items.english: It was not that the council misread the complaints, but that it did not want to listen to them.

sections.content: English uses the same verb form in both halves: "It's not that he *is* wrong, it's that he *is* late." In Spanish the first verb after *No es que* is in the subjunctive and the verb after *sino que* is in the indicative. And *sino* needs its *que* before a conjugated verb: *No es que lo rechace, sino que lo aplaza*, never *sino lo aplaza*.
